title: Automatic Transmission Controls: A Component Map
introduction:
The cabin selector, its cable and the steering-wheel paddles are different parts of the driver’s transmission controls. I use these drawings like a route map: first find the control you touch, then follow the drawing toward the components connected with it.

In the selector view, the knob sits above the bezel and selector assembly. The cable curves from that assembly toward the transmission, with its adjuster identified near the transmission end. The brake shift interlock actuator is identified at the selector assembly. The separate steering-wheel view places the downshift paddle on the left and the upshift paddle on the right as shown.

Match each callout to the table immediately beside its drawing; the callout sequence restarts in the paddle view. This map establishes component identity and location relationships. It does not provide trim access, cable adjustment, interlock override, switch testing or removal instructions.

edits.why: I follow the cable’s curved route between the cabin selector assembly and the transmission, then use the leader lines to distinguish the cable adjuster from its surrounding attachments. Identifying an adjuster is not an instruction to release it.

Use this drawing’s own table to distinguish downshift from upshift. The wheel is shown from the driver-facing side; the illustration identifies the paddles without showing their attachment or electrical connections.
